correctness.rationale: The canonical signed-Gamma HBB transform gives the explicit two-dimensional gamma-ray Lévy kernel. Truncated Thorin-measure approximations converge jointly by the Fourier-Laplace identity; the Lévy-kernel integrability is established using the standard logarithmic and inverse-square Thorin bounds, and the Gaussian covariance is preserved. A bijective ray-rate map yields exact spectral inversion. Under the added finite first-moment condition, the conditional regression identity is equivalent to vanishing Stieltjes transforms of weighted signed spectral measures, which uniquely implies the exact measure balance. Converse follows from uniqueness of Laplace transforms of finite signed conditional-mean measures. Independence and one-sided association are proved separately by Lévy uniqueness and monotone common jumps. The checker passed 722 finite diagnostic groups. No finite test is presented as an infinite proof.

Searches of research records for equivalent regression, signed spectral balance, and gamma Lévy rays found no decisive covered implication. Historical priority remains nonexhaustive, particularly for general common-jump Lévy regression theories.

value.rationale: The natural question of when a positive latent component predicts the signed coordinate affinely is fully answered for every integrable Thorin spectrum, not only finite atomic mixtures. One-sided spectra are rigid (one magnitude), while genuinely asymmetric two-sided non-atomic measures permit exactly affine conditional prediction; the proof gives necessary and sufficient measure equations and a parameterization of all possibilities. The joint Lévy inverse identifies signs discarded by the positive marginal, with a Gaussian-only independence boundary. This is a structural classification rather than a small numerical gain or a textbook restatement.
